problem: Existing LLM-based zero-shot visual semantic (object) navigation frameworks rely on a single LLM for commonsense reasoning, which makes decisions fragile in dynamic, complex environments.
motivation: Effective navigation depends on commonsense such as room-object topological relationships, and LLMs supply this knowledge. A single LLM is brittle when it has to analyze the scene, verify observations, plan and reflect all at once, so splitting these roles across specialized experts could give more robust frontier decisions.
key_idea: A multi-expert LLM framework in which four experts (indoor environment analysis, visual semantic verification, comprehensive navigation planning, decision reflection) coordinate through shared environmental states to progressively refine zero-shot navigation frontier choices.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The paper's claim is that decomposing navigation reasoning into specialized, mutually checking experts with reflection improves robustness over single-LLM decision making.
method: Indoor environment analysis expert: interprets the environment and room-object topology to provide commonsense priors.
Visual semantic verification expert: verifies observed visual semantics, such as whether the target or related objects are present.
Comprehensive navigation planning expert: integrates the other experts' outputs to select navigation frontiers.
Decision reflection expert: reviews and corrects decisions to progressively optimize them in dynamic environments.
Shared environmental state: the medium through which the experts coordinate and exchange domain-specific knowledge.

setting.backbone: LLM-based experts (specific models not stated in the abstract)
setting.observation: not stated in the abstract (likely egocentric RGB-D)

results: The abstract states that MENav significantly outperforms baseline models in navigation success rate in a zero-shot manner on a reconstructed ProcTHOR-based dataset. No specific numbers or baseline names are given.
limitations: Evaluated on a reconstructed ProcTHOR-based dataset only, according to the abstract.
Multiple LLM experts probably raise inference cost and latency; the abstract does not discuss this.
builds_on: LLM-based zero-shot object navigation with frontier exploration
